### Niche

A localized area of tissue in the body — encompassing both cells and extracellular tissues — that either supports normal cell function (a healthy niche) or becomes permissive to cancer development (a cancer niche). The cancer state is described as arising when a healthy tissue niche breaks down and transforms into a cancer niche.

### Extended Evolutionary Synthesis (EES)

A set of recent extensions to the modern synthesis of evolutionary theory that emphasizes the role of developmental processes occurring within an organism's lifetime, and holds that dysfunctions in evolutionary programs cannot be reduced to dysfunction in genes alone.

### Stigmergy

A systems concept, originally developed in the study of social insects, that describes how the self-organization of collective communities of agents produces the emergent structures of complex systems.

### Allostatic Load

The cumulative duration and persistence of a stress-activated physiological response. In the transcript, a brief, task-appropriate stress response (e.g., climbing stairs) is distinguished from a prolonged, unrelieved response; it is the latter — the persisting allostatic load — that is associated with pathophysiological changes relevant to cancer progression.

### Emergent Features

Properties or behaviors that arise from the collective, interactive behavior of a system's components and that cannot be explained by studying individual parts (such as driver genes) in isolation. The term is used to contrast a systems-level view of cancer with a reductionistic, gene-centered view.

### Extracellular Matrix / Tissue Microenvironment

The structural and biochemical surroundings outside of cells, identified through Mena Bissell's research as playing a central role in determining cell morphology and tissue-specific gene expression. In the transcript, understanding this environment is treated as equally important as understanding the cells themselves.

### Morphogenesis Gone Awry

A framing of cancer growth as a disrupted developmental process rather than simply a product of defective genes. The speaker extends this framing analogically to conditions such as schizophrenia, suggesting that developmental programs, not genes alone, are the relevant unit of analysis.

### Autonomic Nervous System (ANS) / Neuroendocrine Signaling

The peripheral autonomic nervous system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal neuroendocrine axis, described in the transcript as recently recognized regulators of tumor progression. Their molecular roles — including effects on inflammation, hematopoietic homeostasis, and metastasis — are presented as a mechanism linking chronic stress to cancer outcomes.

### Holobiotic Milieu

The assemblage of eukaryotic cells and symbiotic microorganisms that together constitute an individual's biological context. In the transcript, the cancer state is described as evolving within this milieu, making what counts as biological "self" both dynamic and highly context-dependent.

### Modern Synthesis

The earlier integration of Darwinian natural selection with genetics, which explained evolution through genetic variability and natural selection alone. It is presented in the transcript as the baseline from which the Extended Evolutionary Synthesis departs by incorporating developmental and environmental processes.
